text: [serious, cinematic storyteller, brisk pace] The world doesn't end with a bang. It ends slowly… one ordinary morning at a time. This city wakes before the sun. Kitchen lights flicker on. Engines cough awake. The call to prayer rises over a hundred phone alarms. By seven, the streets are full. Millions of people. One goal: survive one more day. The towers keep rising. From the top, the people below are just dots. The news moves faster now. An earthquake here. A war there. Whole peoples wiped out, while the world watches. A life taken over almost nothing. A man trusted with everything… betrays it all. Read. Swipe. Forgotten. And the days feel shorter. Morning starts… and suddenly, it's night again. Nothing seems wrong. But all of this, towers racing for the sky, trust placed in the wrong hands, the earth shaking again and again, killing that no longer shocks anyone, time slipping away, was foretold by the Prophet Muhammad, fourteen hundred years ago. When the end will come, no one knows. Only God. Night falls like any other night. The lights go out, one by one. Tomorrow morning, a message will spread through the entire city… about something that never happened.
